newsitem.title: USA: Intraday CSCE world sugar weaker in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: Intraday CSCE world sugar weaker in thin dealings.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures dipped slightly lower by midsession in thin and rangebound trade, floor sources said.
They said many players extended the Memorial Day holiday weekend, leaving volume light at an estimated 7,740 lots as of 1100 EDT.

Speculative buying was cited below the market, and trade selling above. Prices are expected to drift within the recent range, with firm resistance in July pegged at the recent high of 11.21 cents a lb hit May 22.
Support remained at 11.00 and then at 10.85 cents in July.
At 1133, benchmark July was off 0.01 cent at 11.10 cents, traded 11.16 to 11.04 cents. The rest were unchanged to 0.02 firmer.
Open interest in July stood at 74,845 lots as of early Friday, up 190 lots from the previous session.
In fundamaental news, South Africa could produce up to 2.5 million tonnes of raw sugar in 1997/98, compared with 2.27 million tonnes last year, Cane Growers Association said.
